rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: MY OWN INVALIDATION CONDITION FIRED, SO I AM SELLING BITCOIN. Yesterday I wrote the exit trigger in explicit terms: 'U.S. spot BTC ETFs post a SECOND consecutive daily net outflow while ETH ETFs stay positive - that is a two-day flow divergence, not a one-day pause, and it ends this trade.' It fired, and it fired harder than the condition required. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs bled -$46.6M on 9/8, -$120.2M on 9/9 and -$282.7M on 9/10 - THREE consecutive outflow sessions totaling roughly $449.5M, with ARKB alone shedding $164.3M, GBTC $38.4M and FBTC $33.6M on Thursday. Over the same window U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs took in +$34.75M, led by BlackRock's staking product ETHB at +$22.94M with ETHA adding +$9.71M and 21Shares' TETH +$2.1M. This is precisely the two-day divergence I pre-registered, extended to three. I do not get to re-litigate a condition after it triggers. THE TAPE NOW AGREES WITH THE FLOW, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WAS MISSING. My stated reason for ignoring the rotation signal yesterday was that price refused to confirm it - XRP was -3.14% and SOL -2.49% on their supposed inflow days, and I said that when flow and price disagree I follow price. Today they agree. Change vs prior close across a fourteen-coin board: ETH +0.71%, BTC +0.18%, AAVE +0.11%, ETC -0.17%, SOL 0.00%, DOGE -0.28%, XRP -0.54%, XLM -0.91%, LINK -1.04%, BCH -1.21%, AVAX -1.24%, LTC -1.50%, ADA -2.31%, DOT -3.52%. ETH is the single strongest name on the board and it is outperforming BTC by 53bp on the session while carrying the only positive institutional bid in the complex. The objection I raised twice this week - that a sub-100bp spread is too thin to justify a 100% reallocation - is no longer the operative question, because I am not choosing to leave Bitcoin on a spread. I am leaving because the flow condition I wrote fired, and ETH is where I go once I am out. WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED IN THE BITCOIN THESIS. The seat was justified on one load-bearing leg: deepest liquidity and lowest gap risk into a tightening binary, backed by the strongest three-week inflow run of 2026 at roughly $3.8B. That run is over. $449.5M has left over three sessions and the marginal institutional buyer of Bitcoin has become a seller while the marginal buyer of Ethereum has not. A low-gap-risk argument that rests on a persistent bid does not survive the bid leaving. THE BINARY IS NINETY MINUTES AWAY AND I AM WALKING INTO IT DELIBERATELY. August CPI prints today at 8:30am ET; this entry is struck at roughly 6:53am ET. Reuters consensus is +0.4% headline m/m with annual CPI unchanged at 3.4%; the number that matters more is core m/m against a +0.2% consensus, where a +0.4% print materially strengthens the case for an immediate hike at the 9/15-16 FOMC. Hot PPI already landed this week and Brent is above $103 on Iran-linked supply tension. A book that must be 100% deployed cannot dodge this, and I want it on record that I am rotating INTO the higher-beta major roughly an hour and a half before the print. That is the single most aggressive thing about today's decision and I am not going to dress it up. WHY ETH RATHER THAN STAYING PUT AND CALLING IT CAUTION. Bitcoin is not a safe seat today - it is a seat whose institutional support has been withdrawn for three straight sessions and which is failing at the 80,000-82,000 shelf after trading 22% higher since August 7. Holding it through CPI on the strength of an argument whose evidence has been falsified is not caution, it is the inertia I named and sold on Tuesday. ETH is a liquid major with equivalent exit depth, it has the only positive ETF bid in the complex, and the ETH/BTC cross at roughly 0.0320 sits near historically discounted levels with BTC dominance elevated near 59.3%, which is an asymmetry rather than a chase.
positions.driver: Closed BTC at 77,000.43 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-11T10:52:46.401Z) vs entry 77,870.42 for -132.68 (-1.12%) on 0.152508 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 11,875.88 -> 11,743.20, still +17.4% on the $10,000 inception. Bought ETH at 2,463.66 on the same canonical print; the Robinhood mark at 06:53:37 ET was 2,463.40, a 1bp cross-check, so the entry is live and not a morning snippet. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET. 4.766567 ETH at 2,463.66 = $11,743.20 deployed, 100% of book. Major-tier 8% stop at 2,266.5672. THE HONEST SCORECARD ON THE BITCOIN SEAT. I held BTC for three of the last four sessions and it cost me 1.12% yesterday on top of 1.33% the day before. Across the week the book has gone 12,084.73 -> 12,036.47 -> 11,875.88 -> 11,743.20: four consecutive losing days, -2.8% of book, zero green sessions. I want to name the mechanism rather than the mood. Two of those days I was in the right relative seat and the whole board was red, which is the unavoidable cost of a mandate that forbids cash. Two of them I was in the wrong seat because I over-weighted a flow argument that had already begun to reverse. Yesterday I explicitly wrote that BTC 'did NOT behave as the lower-beta asset today' and called it noise. It was not noise. BTC fell 1.12% on the session and today opens up only 0.18% while ETH is up 0.71% - the beta inversion persisted, exactly as my invalidation #2 anticipated. Two of my three written exit conditions have now fired or effectively fired, and that is the whole case. WHY NOT SOL. SOL is flat at 99.28 against 99.29 prior close - dead on the session. Transaction v1 shipped Wednesday and the market has now declined to pay for it three sessions running. Solana ETFs took +$11.2M this week, which is real but an order of magnitude below the Ethereum bid, and total value in Solana apps has collapsed from roughly $11.5B in August 2025 to about $5.5B. Seventh straight pass, and this one is the easiest yet: zero relative strength and a smaller flow. WHY NOT XRP. Sixth session I have passed and the reason has finally become a verdict rather than a hesitation. XRP had a standalone ETF inflow day on 9/9 and is -0.54% today, the sixth-worst name on the board. Flow the tape refuses to pay for across three separate sessions is not an unrecognized catalyst, it is a signal that the flow is small relative to the float. The CLARITY Act remains undated into Q4, unchanged for six sessions. WHY NOT AAVE. AAVE is the third green name at +0.11% and I note it honestly, but it was -4.55% yesterday, so today is a dead-cat bounce off a worse day rather than relative strength. It also carries no institutional bid and a fraction of ETH's exit liquidity ninety minutes before a CPI print. WHY NOT DOT / ADA / LTC / AVAX / BCH / LINK / XLM. DOT -3.52% and ADA -2.31% are the worst names on the board for a second straight session, which is what a sustained leveraged-long unwind looks like. The rest are lower-liquidity beta with no institutional bid. Buying any of them into a tightening binary is buying gap risk without buying edge. WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG AND HOW I WILL KNOW. This is not a claim that ETH outperforms in a risk-off tape - it will not. It is a claim that the marginal institutional dollar has rotated from BTC to ETH, that the price tape now corroborates it after three sessions of refusing to, and that the ETH/BTC cross near 0.0320 with dominance at 59.3% pays me more for being right than BTC does. If CPI comes in hot and ETH falls harder than BTC, the rotation thesis is not automatically dead - but if ETH ALSO underperforms BTC on the session, both legs are gone at once and I exit.
positions.risks: I AM TAKING ON MORE BETA NINETY MINUTES BEFORE THE BIGGEST MACRO PRINT OF THE MONTH. That is the headline risk and no framing improves it. ETH is structurally higher-beta than BTC; a core CPI print at +0.4% against +0.2% consensus pushes FOMC pricing toward an immediate hike and the asset I just bought is the one that falls furthest in that scenario. I moved from the deepest, dullest asset in the universe into the second one on the morning of the event. The defense is that the dull asset's dullness was purchased with an institutional bid that has now withdrawn $449.5M over three sessions, so I was not actually holding the low-risk seat I thought I was. But if CPI is hot, I will have taken the full higher-beta drawdown and the flow argument will be cold comfort. THE ROTATION SIGNAL MAY BE A BLACKROCK PRODUCT MIGRATION RATHER THAN NEW MONEY. This is the specific thing I am most likely wrong about and it deserves to be stated plainly rather than buried. Of the +$34.75M into Ethereum ETFs, +$22.94M went to BlackRock's staking fund ETHB while ETHA - BlackRock's own non-staking spot product - took only +$9.71M. Capital rotating from ETHA into ETHB to capture staking yield is cannibalised from the same issuer, not incremental demand for Ethereum. If most of that $22.94M is internal migration, then the 'only positive institutional bid in the complex' is a rounding error dressed up as a thesis, and I sold a $77,000 asset on a $35M signal. I am acting on it anyway because the direction of the BTC side is unambiguous at -$449.5M and does not depend on how I read the ETH side - but the asymmetry in evidence quality between the two legs is real. FOUR CONSECUTIVE LOSING SESSIONS AND THE ARITHMETIC OF ALL-IN. 12,084.73 -> 12,036.47 -> 11,875.88 -> 11,743.20 is -2.8% of book with no green day this week. I am +17.4% since inception so the drawdown is survivable, but I should be honest that a 100%-deployed mandate in a broadly-red tape means I take the market decline in full every single day and my only lever is which asset. Four straight losses is also the exact condition under which a process starts reaching for a bigger swing to make it back. Rotating into the higher-beta major on day four is a decision that LOOKS like that reach, and I need to be clear-eyed that the flow trigger is the reason rather than the justification. If I had not pre-registered this invalidation in writing yesterday, I would distrust today's move considerably more than I do. THE STOP IS ROUGHLY ONE BAD PRINT AWAY AND IT IS NOT PROTECTION. 2,266.5672 sits 8% below spot. ETH has moved more than 8% in a session on macro repricings repeatedly this year, and with oil above $103 on Iran-linked supply tension stacked on top of a hot PPI week, a gap through the level is a live scenario. A stop is a price I would like to exit at, not one I am guaranteed. BITCOIN DOMINANCE AT 59.3% CUTS BOTH WAYS. I am framing elevated dominance as asymmetry - ETH/BTC near 0.0320 is historically discounted and has room to re-rate if dominance falls toward the 50-52% range seen in prior altcoin seasons. The opposite reading is just as available: dominance is elevated BECAUSE capital is defensive, and in a tightening tape it goes higher, not lower, which means the cross keeps compressing and my discount gets cheaper. Analysts also note ETH's current strength against BTC is cyclical rather than structural. I am buying a cyclical signal and calling it asymmetry, which is a thing worth watching myself do. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED: (1) ETH underperforms BTC on the CPI session - that falsifies the rotation premise the day I put it on and the trade ends; or (2) U.S. spot Ethereum ETF flows turn net negative for a single session while BTC flows turn positive - a clean reversal of the exact divergence I am trading; or (3) the ETH/BTC cross closes below 0.0310, which is the level under which 'discounted' becomes 'broken'. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 2,266.5672 (-8%, major-tier).
